articles.title_orig: Live Updates: Trump, Xi and Putin to Hold First-Ever Joint Meeting at China Summit
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Trump, Xi and Putin to Hold First-Ever Joint Meeting at China Summit
articles.content_orig:
Donald Trump calls Vladimir Putin his "friend" before they hold a meeting with China's President Xi in Shenzhen
Trump held separate, bilateral meetings with Putin and Xi before the three-way talks
One of Putin's aides said the bilateral meeting with Trump went "well", with Putin in an "excellent mood"
After meeting Xi, Trump said the US and China want to see an end to the Ukraine war
In the three-way talks, the leaders are expected to discuss Ukraine, the war in Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions, and AI
There is growing frustration in many European circles that Xi does not put more pressure on Russia over Ukraine, writes Laura Bicker
Edited by Tessa Wong, with Laura Bicker, Steve Rosenberg, Nada Tawfik and Stephen McDonell in Shenzhen, China
Russia's President Vladimir Putin has left his hotel and is enroute to the Kylin Villa, where he'll meet with Trump and Xi, according to China's state broadcaster CCTV.
We're seeing black cars bearing the Russian flag on the road, via CCTV's live feed.
Also keeping a close eye on the trilateral is Taiwan, the self-governed island that China claims as its territory - and has not ruled out taking it by force one day.
Xi reiterated last week that China's reunification with Taiwan "must be realised".
US arms sales to Taiwan has been a major sticking point in US-China relations. Beijing has been pushing for the US to stop selling weapons to Taiwan, while the US has argued those sales are to help Taiwan maintain defensive capability.
Taiwan said on Wednesday that it was in "close contact" with the US ahead of the trilateral talks.
Taiwan is a full member of Apec, which considers its members by economies rather than countries - an arrangement which allows Taiwan to participate at the forum while skirting around the thorny issue of Taiwan sovereignty.
We've reported earlier that Xi was preparing to host the trilateral with Trump and Putin, but it appears he's having lunch now with Trump at the Kylin Villa, according to the press pool traveling with the US president.
It's now past 15:30 in Shenzhen, and it looks like their schedule is extremely delayed.
Three-way talks between Xi, Trump and Putin have yet to begin - we'll bring you updates on that once we have them.
Laura Bicker China correspondent
More than once have I heard US and European officials state that China could help end the war in Ukraine if it wanted to.
Beijing is accused of helping provide components that Vladimir Putin can use in the war and of aiding Moscow's economy by buying Russian oil and gas.
China has tried to maintain that it is neutral in this war, but Xi has refused to condemn his âold friendâ Putin for the invasion.
There is growing frustration in many European circles that Xi does not put more pressure on Russia.
Itâs a tricky balance for China. It will want an end to the war to get the subject off the table and try to bring about more stability in Europe, but Xi will also not want his friend, neighbour and ally to lose, which could trigger instability in Russia.
Thatâs partly why China is resisting any push to put the Ukraine war on the agenda at these talks. But with both Trump and Putin stating publicly that it will be a talking point, it may be a difficult subject for Xi to avoid.
We're bringing you more lines from the Trump-Xi bilateral, which wrapped up earlier this afternoon.
Xi had compared the transformation of Shenzhen, the southern city hosting the Apec summit, to US-China relations. "In the space of just over 40 years, a small fishing village has grown into an international metropolis," Xi told Trump.
What lies behind the transformation is the courage to "break new ground, to experiment and to take the lead", he said. "And of course, it also means putting in the hard work."
In a similar vein, building a "constructive China-US relationship" is also a "pioneering undertaking without precedent", he added.
"It too requires us to dare to break new ground and experiment, to keep our feet on the ground and to see our work through to a successful conclusion."
The success of Shenzhen, which is China's tech hub, was hailed by Xi yesterday during his address to business and political leaders around the world yesterday.
While we wait for the trilateral to begin, here are some humanoid robots doing ballet.
Earlier today at the Apec leaders summit, a cyborg troupe performed for delegates - though they weren't quite en pointe.
Humanoid robots dance ballet at Apec
Xi Jinping is about to hold the historic trilateral with Trump and Putin, according to Chinese state media CCTV.
We'll bring you more updates shortly.
Much has been said about the upcoming trilateral meeting possibly becoming a "Yalta 2.0" conference where Xi, Trump and Putin would carve up spheres of influence and decide the fate of smaller countries.
The original Yalta conference saw the leaders of the US, UK and Soviet Union meeting in the Crimea resort city in 1945 to discuss the post-war reorganisation of Europe.
In the lead-up to today's meeting, however, Chinese media and scholars have pushed back against such a comparison, calling it "outdated Cold War thinking".
Some have argued that any Yalta-style arrangement during the trilateral summit would run counter to the existing international order with the United Nations as the core,  as well as Chinaâs push for a multipolar world and greater democracy in international relations.
The Chinese foreign ministry has repeatedly declined to offer more details on the talks, only giving broad lines that they will have "in-depth exchange of views on important issues bearing on global peace".
Winston Churchill, Franklin D Roosevelt, and Joseph Stalin in Yalta in 1945
Liza Fokht BBC News Russian
Putin looked cheerful after his meeting with Trump
Vladimir
Putin is âin an excellent moodâ following his meeting with Donald Trump,
according to his top foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov.
Speaking
to Russian state TV channel Vesti, Ushakov described the talks between the
presidents as having gone âwell.â
Russian
media have widely shared footage of Trump entering the room and addressing
Putin with the words: âWho is he? He's my friend!â
According to Ushakov, the war in Ukraine was the main topic of the
meeting, which lasted 35 to 40 minutes. The two leaders also discussed US-Russia
bilateral relations.
The
Kremlin claims that neither president made any âmajor statementsâ as both sides
are preparing for a summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping later today.
Steve Rosenberg Russia editor
Ahead of this trilateral weâve heard plenty of superlatives about this meeting from the parties involved.
Labels such as âhistoricâ and âgroundbreakingâ. The Kremlin bigged it up as âthe show stopperâ event in Shenzhen this week.
But as the build-up comes to an end, the question is: will this mini summit produce any concrete results? Or will it be case of symbolism over substance?
The Russians already see it as a diplomatic victory: a top table discussion that allows Vladimir Putin to rub shoulders with the leaders of great powers, despite Russiaâs ongoing war on Ukraine.
The bilateral meeting between Trump and Xi has ended, Chinese state media CCTV reports.
We'll bring you more updates as we get them - especially on the trilateral with Putin later.
Laura Bicker China correspondent
President Xi has described US-China relations as stable and
improving as he met with Donald Trump in Shenzhen.
He added that he was willing to continue to work with the US
president to continue to steer relations between the two superpowers on the
correct course.
Xi needs a stable relationship with the US right now as Chinaâs
economy is heavily reliant on exports. He wonât want a return to the soaring
tariffs that almost brought trade between the two powers to a standstill.
Trump added that he hoped to discuss ending the Ukraine war with
Xi later when both of them meet with Vladimir Putin.

articles.title_zh: Trump says US, China spy on each other, claims Washington does it better
articles.content_orig:
This blog is now closed, you can read more on this story here
The Associated Press is reporting that Donald Trump plans to hold a meeting with Vladimir Putin on Thursday, citing an anonymous US official. The meeting would be in addition to the blockbuster trilateral talks the two will hold with host Xi Jinping on Thursday.
Meanwhile, a meeting between the leaders of China, the United States and Russia planned for Thursday in Shenzhen is set to last less than 60 minutes, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media on Wednesday. “No more than an hour” has been set aside for the historic summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, Peskov was quoted as saying by Russian state news agencies.
Xi Jinping told Donald Trump he hoped their talks would help advance a “constructive, strategic and stable relationship” between China and the US, based on “respect, fairness and reciprocity”, according to China’s state news agency Xinhua . Xi also recalled Trump’s personal welcome at the airport during his visit to the US in September, saying China’s own welcome for the US president reflected its tradition of reciprocity.
Xi personally greeted Trump on the airport tarmac in Shenzhen , reciprocating the welcome the US president extended to the Chinese leader during his visit to the US in September.
Before landing in Shenzhen, Donald Trump enjoyed lunch in Manila with Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr at the Malacañang presidential palace. Speaking during a meeting ahead of lunch, Marcos revealed that he had arranged for fried chicken from Filipino fast food chain Jollibee to be delivered to the US delegation as a late-night snack last night, praising Trump for “working very hard”.
Chinese state media have released a readout of Xi Jinping’s earlier meeting with Vladimir Putin . In it, Xi is quoted as saying China-Russia relations are “unshaken by storms and steady as a mountain”, and have set “an example of a new type of major-country relationship characterised by equality, mutual respect, trustworthiness, and win-win co-operation”.
Canada’s Mark Carney has hit back at Vladimir Putin’s earlier assertion that sanctions no longer work in this day and age. “Mr Putin can ask his financial institutions, he can ask his oligarch friends, he can ask his hockey players whether or not sanctions are a thing of the past. I think he’ll find out that they’re very real, they’re biting,” Carney told reporters.
Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum won praise and went viral on Chinese social media on Wednesday for taking an economy flight to attend a regional summit in Shenzhen. World leaders this week descended on the southern Chinese city to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings – many arriving in specially chartered commercial airliners or dedicated government aircraft like US president Donald Trump’s Air Force One.
It is unclear whether North Korean leader Kim Jong-un will attend the talks, but Trump has floated the possibility. On Wednesday US secretary of state Marco Rubio said the US president was willing to engage, but he did not confirm whether a meeting had been set in Shenzhen.
Trump said on Wednesday that the US has just ⁠concluded a “very big ⁠trade ​deal” with the Philippines, but he did not provide any details, and Manila ⁠did not announce any agreement. “We’ve just consummated a very big trade deal, the ⁠biggest trade deal we’ve ever made so far, and it ​is a fair ‌deal for both countries,” ‌Trump said during a state luncheon at the Philippine ‌presidential palace. Trump is set to arrive in Shenzhen on Wednesday evening.
Trump landed in China on Wednesday seeking to reinforce America’s status as the world’s leading technology power, but a distressing series of technical outages back home has left his administration scrambling to calm the US public.
The issues put the administration on the defensive at a moment when the president wants to project strength and certainty before the meeting with Xi and Putin.
As he began his trip to Asia, Trump initially had been nonchalant about the outages that left people in the US worried about accessing their email, checking their bank accounts or safely flying on an airplane.
“It’s fine,” Trump said Tuesday from the Philippine capital of Manila, suggesting it was all just a consequence of being a nation that is “big and powerful.”
The meeting between the leaders of China , the United States and Russia planned for Thursday in Shenzhen is set to last less than 60 minutes, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media.
“No more than an hour” has been set aside for the historic summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin , Peskov was quoted as saying by Russian state news agencies.
The Associated Press is reporting that Donald Trump plans to hold a separate meeting with Vladimir Putin on Thursday, citing an anonymous US official.
The meeting would be in addition to the blockbuster trilateral talks the two will hold with host Xi Jinping on Thursday.
If confirmed, it would be their first bilateral since they met in Alaska in 2025 for talks that failed to reach a deal on the war in Ukraine.
Trump had already suggested he might meet with Putin, as well as with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, but neither option had been added to his official schedule.
Before landing in Shenzhen, Donald Trump enjoyed lunch in Manila with Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr at the Malacañang presidential palace.
Speaking during a meeting ahead of lunch, Marcos revealed that he had arranged for fried chicken from Filipino fast food chain Jollibee to be delivered to the US delegation as a late-night snack last night, praising Trump for “working very hard”.
The gift may have gone down particularly well with Trump, who has something of a reputation for his love of fast food. The US president has long been associated with McDonald’s and KFC, with his former campaign aides revealing in 2017 that his usual McDonald’s order included two Big Macs, two Filet-O-Fish sandwiches and a chocolate milkshake. The Guardian reported on their revelations at the time in this article:
Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum won praise and went viral on Chinese social media on Wednesday for taking an economy flight to attend a regional summit in Shenzhen.
World leaders this week descended on the southern Chinese city to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings – many arriving in specially chartered commercial airliners or dedicated government aircraft like US president Donald Trump’s Air Force One.
Sheinbaum, however, flew in economy class from Mexico City to Shenzhen on a China Southern Airlines flight, media reports said. She arrived in China on Monday.
Posts on Chinese social media platform Weibo showed the Mexican leader in the plane chatting with passengers, though the photos could not be independently verified by AFP. A hashtag on Weibo about her arrival in China garnered 10.2m views as of Wednesday.
Meanwhile, Sheinbaum said ​on Wednesday she had a “very good ⁠meeting” with her US counterpart Trump ⁠as the two ​countries ‌pursue negotiations aimed ‌at easing trade tensions.
“We ‌continue to make progress on our shared agenda,” Sheinbaum added in a post on ‌X.
The Canadian prime minister’s office has issued a statement following Mark Carney’s meeting with US president Donald Trump on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen.
double quotation mark This evening, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, met with the President of the United States, Donald J. Trump, on the margins of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting, in Shenzhen, China.
The leaders discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement that would create good jobs, boost affordability, and fully respect Canada’s languages, culture, and sovereignty. They agreed to continue the work and to stay in close contact.

articles.content_orig:
This live blog is now closed.
Follow our live coverage of the Asia-Pacific economic cooperation summit
Sign up for US breaking News email
Speaking with Fox news, Donald Trump said he wasn’t worried about multiple outages this week affecting Microsoft, US banks, United Airlines computers, the National Security Agency’s internal comms network, Apple services and the national air traffic control system.
“They’re all individual events. These are big companies. They’re putting in new equipment and things happen when you put in new equipment. And these are all individual things,” he said.
When asked whether he raised the issue of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman suspected of being a spy for China with Xi, Trump said he “might’ve referred to it just briefly”
“Because it’s such a tragedy. It’s a tragedy. He’s such a brilliant man ... we have to take care of our geniuses,” Trump said of Huang.
Of Alice Huang, Jensen Huang’s affair partner, the president mused: “I haven’t heard that she was a spy. She was a business woman who bought chips. Who knows if they were bought right or wrong. But I can tell you we allow them to buy. We want to make money.”
However, according to a report by the New York Times, Trump was briefed aboard Air Force One in May en route to China that the US intelligence showed that that Nvidia’s chief executive was in a relationship with a woman thought to be a Chinese spy.
Trump also shrugged off the Fox reporter’s question about whether he would confront China over spying allegations.
“We spy on them too”, he said. “I think we spy better than they do.”
A historic trilateral meeting is taking place in China between US president Donald Trump, China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin. The leaders will be discussing Russia’s war with Ukraine, the US war in Iran, as well as global trade, AI, and nuclear weapons. Plus, the subject of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang being embroiled in a spy scandal has only come up “briefly” so far between Trump and Xi Jinping.
House Democrats have nominated current minority leader Hakeem Jeffries as their candidate for speaker in the next Congress. Jeffries received 251 yes votes of 262 cast, and 11 members voted no on his nomination. He faced no challengers but it will lead to a full chamber vote in the new year when Democrats are in the majority. Jeffries is poised to be the first Black speaker in US history.
During a fiery House hearing, Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, defended his decision to take a government plane to attend a college football game, while thousands of flights had been cancelled and the airspace closed during the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) nationwide grounding over the weekend. “You want to bring up the fact that I took my family and my great nieces to an [Lousiana State University] game that was scheduled for weeks prior because I wanted to be a good uncle,” Mullin said, following questions from Congressman Bennie Thompson, the homeland security committee’s top Democrat. Mullin went further, and said that had he not traveled to the game it could have created “confusion” because he was due to meet Louisiana governor Jeff Landry. Mullin added that his absence might have shown “distrust that we’re not even willing to fly” after the FAA reopened the airspace.
Elon Musk called his midterm political spending “foolish. ” After pouring nearly half a billion dollars into the election, in a Wednesday conversation with The New York Times’s DealBook Summit, Musk said: “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.”
US Transportation secretary Sean Duffy blamed contractor L3Harris for last week’s nationwide ground stop. As legislators press for more answers on last week’s outage that caused thousands of flights to be halted, Duffy has continued finger-pointing, telling digital media outlet 2WAY on Wednesday that L3Harris, the aerospace and defense company whose router malfunctioned during an update, did not identify the issue “quick enough.”
Trump’s contentious triumphal arch continues to face setbacks. A federal judge extended the construction ban for the arch, slated for the Memorial Circle in Washington DC. A group of veterans and members of the Kennedy family members have blasted the project as disrespectful to those interred at the Arlington national cemetery.
Alaska Republican representative Nick Begich has retained his seat, according to the Associated Press. The call was made Wednesday evening after the state’s ranked choice tabulation, a process that occurs when candidates do not receive over 50% of the vote.
Ultimately, Begich, a Trump-backed millionaire, secured 51.35% of the vote, besting his independent challenger Bill Hill, a fisherman who ran on a message of affordability, as Alaskans weather soaring energy prices. Hill received 48.65%.
The race also included a Democrat, Eric Hafner, an apparent spoiler candidate, who advanced in the primary, despite being incarcerated in federal prison.
Hill said on X that he called Begich to congratulate his opponent on the win.
“This campaign has always been about taking power back from DC elites and putting it in the hands of the hardworking people of Alaska,” he wrote. “While we did not prevail in this election, we will continue that fight together.”
US president Donald Trump , China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin are set to engage in trilateral talks, a blockbuster diplomatic event for the three countries.
On the agenda is Russia’s war with Ukraine , the US war in Iran , as well as global trade, AI, and nuclear weapons .
Trump arrived at the Asia-Pacific economic corporation (Apec) meeting in Shenzhen, China on Thursday morning local time, pausing for photographs on a red carpet, the only leader to do so.
Member states of Apec took a family photo, as they donned red and blue silk scarves.

Donald Trump, who repeatedly prophesied an apocalyptic future if Democrats regained control of Congress, has changed his tune, telling Fox News the next two years will be “unbelievably productive.”
He suggested he would be liberal with his veto power, but also open to cutting deals across the party line.
“They’ll send me a bill on health care and I’ll say no way and I’ll veto it. And then, they’ll call me and we’ll sit down. That’s what I do,” Trump said on Wednesday. “Politics is a nasty game. They won.”
Donald Trump will reportedly meet one-on-one with Vladimir Putin , the prime minister of Russia, during his Asia summit.
When asked by Fox News if he mentioned the bilateral meeting to Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump appeared to sidestep the question.
“They got to get along,” Trump replied, referring to Zelenskyy and Putin, whose countries remain at war. “If I were president, if the election weren’t rigged, that war would’ve never happened,” he added, repeating a baseless election fraud theory.
Since February 2022, when Putin ordered the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by Russian forces, nearly 18,000 citizens have been killed and 58,000 injured, according to estimates from the United Nations.
Trump then offered a wildly inflated death toll for the conflict, claiming that “probably two million people, mostly soldiers, are dead.” In fact, more than 400,000 Russians have been killed fighting in Ukraine since Russia’s full-scale invasion, according to leaked data from the state statistics agency, Rosstat. In July, the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated that between 125,000 and 150,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed.
“It’s a shame. It’s so sad. It doesn’t affect us,” Trump told Fox News. He noted that the US has sold military equipment to the European Union, which provides it to Ukrainian forces, in contrast to what he framed as handouts from his predecessor Joe Biden ’s administration. articles.title_orig: Asian Stocks Set to Fall Ahead of Anthropic Debut: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Asian Stocks Set to Fall Ahead of Anthropic Debut: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic said Wednesday it is selling shares in its initial public offering at an even higher price than previously marketed, setting it up for the largest Wall Street debut of all time.
Anthropic confirmed the IPO includes a sale of 980 million shares at $83 a share, raising $81.3 billion — surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion IPO as the biggest on record.
The IPO is a major event for Wall Street and a pivotal moment for the artificial intelligence boom that has become a driving force behind the stock market.
The final pricing comes after Anthropic spent the past few days pitching its public offering to different investors. Anthropic initially set a target range for its shares at $70 to $78 a share, but the new pricing above the original range signals strong investor demand. Anthropic also raised the total number of shares being sold, up from 825 million.
Anthropic is selling roughly 956 million shares, while the company’s seven co-founders are selling roughly 24 million shares total, bringing the total number of shares to 980 million.
Anthropic is set to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker “ ANT .” At $83 a share, the company’s valuation could be around $1.5 trillion — an enormous figure for a company founded barely six years ago, reflecting the excitement around AI.
The strong IPO pricing comes despite recent market jitters. The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite has dropped more than 10% since its record high; and Nvidia, which has been a major component of the AI trade, is down 30% in the past month. Investors have been looking for signs of strength especially since the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who left after admitting to an extramarital affair.
The IPO price is set by the company and the bankers underwriting the offering after gauging investors’ interest, and it’s what investors participating in the public offering will pay. But it’s not necessarily the price people will be paying when the stock hits the market.
Anthropic’s Wall Street debut marks a new chapter for AI
The opening price of the stock is determined based on the fundamentals of supply and demand. For example, SpaceX set its IPO price at $135 a share, and opened on the stock market at $150 a share . Once trading begins, the price will fluctuate.
Investors at major institutions and financial firms often participate in IPOs, and they get first dibs on the shares. That’s not to say that retail investors who don’t work buying stocks for big companies will be left out in the cold. Companies can set aside shares for retail investors — or everyday people who trade or buy stocks in their own brokerage accounts — in IPOs. Anthropic is no different, and it’s set to put aside 20% of its offering for retail investors.

articles.title_orig: Xi says China-Russia relations bring stability, certainty to turbulent world
articles.title_zh: Xi says China-Russia relations bring stability, certainty to turbulent world
articles.content_orig:
C hinese President Xi Jinping meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. [Photo/Xinhua]
SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Wednesday that China-Russia relations have brought greater stability and certainty to a world of turbulence and transformation.
Xi made the remarks while meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19.
Xi noted that this year marks the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation.
He said that China-Russia ties set an example for a new model of major-country relations featuring equality, mutual respect, good faith, and win-win cooperation.
Xi called on both countries to deepen all-round cooperation and firmly uphold the due responsibilities and obligations of major countries to guide and promote a multipolar world and democratization of international relations.
Both sides should leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between their governments, legislatures, militaries and political parties to ensure that the consensus reached by the two heads of state is effectively implemented, Xi said.
Xi called on the two countries to provide a more stable and predictable investment and business environment and protect the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises from both countries.
The development of China and Russia is closely intertwined with that of the Asia-Pacific region, and APEC is an important platform for enhancing cooperation, Xi noted.
China stands ready to work with the Asia-Pacific family, including Russia, to chart a course for the region's prosperity and development and build an Asia-Pacific community together, Xi said.
Putin said he and Xi have held four productive meetings so far this year, helping sustain the sound development momentum in Russia-China relations. High-level exchanges have been close, bilateral trade has reached a new high, and practical cooperation has made substantial progress across various fields, he said.
Russia is willing to strengthen back-to-back strategic coordination with China, expand cooperation in trade, energy, education and other fields, and broaden cultural and people-to-people exchanges to better benefit the two peoples, Putin said.
Russia also stands ready to work with China to promote development and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, advance the process toward a multipolar world and build a more just and equitable global governance system, he added.

articles.title_orig: Palmer Luckey at DealBook: 'China wants Jensen out, so I want him in', and Musk shouldn't have to risk Starlink for Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Palmer Luckey at DealBook: 'China wants Jensen out, so I want him in', and Musk shouldn't have to risk Starlink for Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk believes he’s helped Ukraine stay alive in the war, claiming Russia would have steamrolled the country if SpaceX hadn’t supplied Kyiv with its crucial Starlink satellite internet.
The billionaire tech tycoon touted himself as Kyiv’s ultimate private-sector savior, boasting that his Starlink tech gave Ukrainian forces a fighting chance, in a Thursday interview with CNBC .
“I think it would probably be accurate to say that there is no private individual who has helped Ukraine more than I have,” Musk boasted . “I made sure that Starlink was in Ukraine prepositioned ahead of the Russian invasion.”
Musk insisted that Starlink stood as Ukraine’s sole indestructible line of defense when Russian strongman Vladimir Putin sent his troops in.
“And when Russia invaded, they disabled all communications, all cell towers, all fiber cables, and every satellite communication system,” he added.
“There was one system they could not disable, and that was Starlink.”
The SpaceX chief insisted that his telecommunications network remains the only thing holding the war-torn country together.
“If we were to turn off Starlink, the entire Ukrainian front would collapse immediately,” he claimed.
Ukrainian officials cried foul last month over their access to Starlink , when they discovered issues with it involving their drones traveling at speeds of 160 km/h or more. Russian drones at the time were traveling at 400 km/h or higher.
The situation occurred shortly after President Trump announced a controversial diesel deal with Putin.
The billionaire claimed Ukraine had been using the civilian “Net system, Starlink, to carry out drone attacks against Russia” and said SpaceX took action to stop that.
If the Ukrainian military wants to use Starlink for defense operations, Musk said they must work directly through the US government to acquire “Star Shield.”
“It is not meant to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people,” he cautioned.
“If you want to do that, you need to do Star Shield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the US government.”
Musk also maintained he won’t be made responsible for battlefield carnage.
“SpaceX has done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth BY FAR,” he said defiantly on X .
“That said, I have nothing but UTTER CONTEMPT for the virtue-signaling evil warmongers who push for endless slaughter and offer no realistic solution to the conflict.”

articles.title_orig: Takaichi gets chilly reception in China on first Japan leader visit since 2019
articles.title_zh: Takaichi gets chilly reception in China on first Japan leader visit since 2019
articles.content_orig:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a subdued welcome on her first trip to China as premier, signaling Beijing's limited appetite for repairing ties strained by a simmering row over Taiwan.
At gatherings such as this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, protocol details — including who greets a visiting leader at the airport and where they are positioned in official photographs — often convey political messages.
Takaichi was met on the tarmac Wednesday by a retired Chinese diplomat, rather than a serving official, and Japan's ambassador to China, Kenji Kanasugi.
The low-key reception contrasted sharply with the warmer welcomes given to other visiting leaders, including South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, while U.S. President Donald Trump was greeted personally by Chinese President Xi Jinping.
In the leaders' group photo, Takaichi was placed in the back row, off to the side and several places from Xi, who stood alongside Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"Beijing sought to downgrade her official status to that of a head of government rather than a head of state," said Jeremy Chan, senior analyst at Eurasia Group.
During Thursday morning's greeting line, Takaichi spent several minutes trying to talk to the Chinese leader without an interpreter present, while most leaders exchanged handshakes and kept walking.
"It has become increasingly difficult for her to engage in formal or even informal conversations with Xi," said Kei Koga, an associate professor at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore, who sees Takaichi's intention as to still "project the image that she could still communicate with him despite the ongoing tensions."
Takaichi's subdued reception signaled Beijing's lack of enthusiasm to repair ties with Tokyo, analysts said, potentially prolonging China's curbs on critical mineral exports that have gripped Japanese industries for the past year.
"China's frosty reception of Takaichi shows quite clearly that Beijing is not yet ready to forgive her over her remarks about Taiwan," Chan said, expecting the bilateral relationship to remain strained until Takaichi leaves office.
That could leave Japan grappling with continued restrictions on rare earth supplies from China next year, said Tianchen Xu, senior economist at the Economist Intelligence Unit.
Relations deteriorated sharply after Takaichi said in November 2025 that a Taiwan Strait crisis could constitute a situation threatening Japan's survival and warrant a self-defense response.
While the substance broadly aligned with Japan's existing security policy, previous prime ministers had generally avoided stating it so explicitly in a Taiwan scenario.
China reacted angrily and demanded that Takaichi retract the remarks. She has not done so, while stating that the door to dialogue with Beijing remains open, with minimal high-level contact over the past year.
China has since tightened restrictions affecting Japan, including controls on dual-use and rare earth exports with potential military uses. It also discouraged its citizens from traveling to Japan and halted Japanese seafood imports.
Takaichi's visit marked the first trip to China by a Japanese prime minister since Shinzo Abe traveled to Chengdu in December 2019 for a trilateral summit with Chinese and South Korean leaders.
No formal Takaichi-Xi meeting has been publicly scheduled during her visit. Meanwhile, Xi is expected to join Trump and Putin for a historic trilateral gathering on Thursday, alongside a bilateral meeting with Trump.
Takaichi needs to show a "reflection of what she said about Taiwan a year ago," said Huiyao Wang, founder of the Beijing-based Center for China and Globalization, which is often seen as close to Beijing's thinking.
Wang said Tokyo should show greater flexibility, pointing to Trump's comments that the U.S. would avoid getting involved in the Taiwan issue. He argued that Japan holding firm on the issue would not help relations with Beijing.
Such reflection, he said, "would really help to clarify some of those misunderstandings between the two countries."

articles.title_orig: When President Donald Trump meets on Thursday with China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, it could mark a pivot in world history — or become a quickly forgotten photo op.
articles.title_zh: When President Donald Trump meets on Thursday with China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, it could mark a pivot in world history — or become a quickly forgotten photo op.
articles.content_orig:
This blog is now closed, you can read more on this story here
The Associated Press is reporting that Donald Trump plans to hold a meeting with Vladimir Putin on Thursday, citing an anonymous US official. The meeting would be in addition to the blockbuster trilateral talks the two will hold with host Xi Jinping on Thursday.
Meanwhile, a meeting between the leaders of China, the United States and Russia planned for Thursday in Shenzhen is set to last less than 60 minutes, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media on Wednesday. “No more than an hour” has been set aside for the historic summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, Peskov was quoted as saying by Russian state news agencies.
Xi Jinping told Donald Trump he hoped their talks would help advance a “constructive, strategic and stable relationship” between China and the US, based on “respect, fairness and reciprocity”, according to China’s state news agency Xinhua . Xi also recalled Trump’s personal welcome at the airport during his visit to the US in September, saying China’s own welcome for the US president reflected its tradition of reciprocity.
Xi personally greeted Trump on the airport tarmac in Shenzhen , reciprocating the welcome the US president extended to the Chinese leader during his visit to the US in September.
Before landing in Shenzhen, Donald Trump enjoyed lunch in Manila with Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr at the Malacañang presidential palace. Speaking during a meeting ahead of lunch, Marcos revealed that he had arranged for fried chicken from Filipino fast food chain Jollibee to be delivered to the US delegation as a late-night snack last night, praising Trump for “working very hard”.
Chinese state media have released a readout of Xi Jinping’s earlier meeting with Vladimir Putin . In it, Xi is quoted as saying China-Russia relations are “unshaken by storms and steady as a mountain”, and have set “an example of a new type of major-country relationship characterised by equality, mutual respect, trustworthiness, and win-win co-operation”.
Canada’s Mark Carney has hit back at Vladimir Putin’s earlier assertion that sanctions no longer work in this day and age. “Mr Putin can ask his financial institutions, he can ask his oligarch friends, he can ask his hockey players whether or not sanctions are a thing of the past. I think he’ll find out that they’re very real, they’re biting,” Carney told reporters.
Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum won praise and went viral on Chinese social media on Wednesday for taking an economy flight to attend a regional summit in Shenzhen. World leaders this week descended on the southern Chinese city to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings – many arriving in specially chartered commercial airliners or dedicated government aircraft like US president Donald Trump’s Air Force One.
It is unclear whether North Korean leader Kim Jong-un will attend the talks, but Trump has floated the possibility. On Wednesday US secretary of state Marco Rubio said the US president was willing to engage, but he did not confirm whether a meeting had been set in Shenzhen.
Trump said on Wednesday that the US has just ⁠concluded a “very big ⁠trade ​deal” with the Philippines, but he did not provide any details, and Manila ⁠did not announce any agreement. “We’ve just consummated a very big trade deal, the ⁠biggest trade deal we’ve ever made so far, and it ​is a fair ‌deal for both countries,” ‌Trump said during a state luncheon at the Philippine ‌presidential palace. Trump is set to arrive in Shenzhen on Wednesday evening.
Trump landed in China on Wednesday seeking to reinforce America’s status as the world’s leading technology power, but a distressing series of technical outages back home has left his administration scrambling to calm the US public.
The issues put the administration on the defensive at a moment when the president wants to project strength and certainty before the meeting with Xi and Putin.
As he began his trip to Asia, Trump initially had been nonchalant about the outages that left people in the US worried about accessing their email, checking their bank accounts or safely flying on an airplane.
“It’s fine,” Trump said Tuesday from the Philippine capital of Manila, suggesting it was all just a consequence of being a nation that is “big and powerful.”
The meeting between the leaders of China , the United States and Russia planned for Thursday in Shenzhen is set to last less than 60 minutes, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media.
“No more than an hour” has been set aside for the historic summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin , Peskov was quoted as saying by Russian state news agencies.
The Associated Press is reporting that Donald Trump plans to hold a separate meeting with Vladimir Putin on Thursday, citing an anonymous US official.
The meeting would be in addition to the blockbuster trilateral talks the two will hold with host Xi Jinping on Thursday.
If confirmed, it would be their first bilateral since they met in Alaska in 2025 for talks that failed to reach a deal on the war in Ukraine.
Trump had already suggested he might meet with Putin, as well as with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, but neither option had been added to his official schedule.
Before landing in Shenzhen, Donald Trump enjoyed lunch in Manila with Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr at the Malacañang presidential palace.
Speaking during a meeting ahead of lunch, Marcos revealed that he had arranged for fried chicken from Filipino fast food chain Jollibee to be delivered to the US delegation as a late-night snack last night, praising Trump for “working very hard”.
The gift may have gone down particularly well with Trump, who has something of a reputation for his love of fast food. The US president has long been associated with McDonald’s and KFC, with his former campaign aides revealing in 2017 that his usual McDonald’s order included two Big Macs, two Filet-O-Fish sandwiches and a chocolate milkshake. articles.title_orig: Waymo pauses driverless taxis on U.S. freeways after California traffic incidents
articles.title_zh: Waymo pauses driverless taxis on U.S. freeways after California traffic incidents
articles.content_orig:
Waymo is currently restricting its fleet of robotaxis to surface streets after getting into hot water with California over its cars’ driving behavior on highways. Specifically, the software tends to drive into construction zones at speed. As first reported by the San Francisco Business Times , this behavior actually drew the ire of California’s DMV earlier this month, which ordered Waymo to stop driving on Californian highways immediately and until it can convince the DMV that its cars no longer “pose an imminent hazard to public safety.”
This is not Waymo’s first run-in with this problem. In Arizona, Waymo robotaxis did not recognize ramp closure signs on six occasions in Phoenix in April and entered construction zones. A month later in California, seven Waymo robotaxis entered lanes with active construction. In June, Waymo recalled the almost 3,800 robotaxis capable of highway driving. That problem led Waymo to stick to surface streets only in California after the May incidents until late July, when the robotaxis resumed highway operations.
In early July, Waymo told the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration that it began updating the robotaxi software to a version that “improve[s] the recognition of freeway construction zones, more appropriately prioritize[s] construction zones over other freeway hazards, and reduce[s] speed when the AV detects that it may be in a construction zone.”
Waymo also told the government that the updated software is better able to respond to emergency vehicles when in a construction zone and that the company has made “operational changes that better identify and mitigate potential entry into pre-planned construction zones and enable more Remote Assistance capability” if it happens again.
Which it has. Despite the update to improve behavior around emergency vehicles, a video went viral in early November showing a Waymo robotaxi on I-280 driving past a pair of California Highway Patrol cars conducting a rolling roadblock as they held traffic behind a slow-moving construction vehicle. California also says there was an incident in which a Waymo robotaxi entered a construction zone on US 101 near Burlingame.
“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do,” Waymo told Ars. “Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”
Waymo also told Ars it was continuing to work with the various California agencies that regulate transport.
Until the suspension, Waymo was only conducting highway operations in Los Angeles and the Bay Area in California, as well as in Arizona.

articles.title_orig: Worried about an AI bust? So is the Federal Reserve.
articles.title_zh: Worried about an AI bust? So is the Federal Reserve.
articles.content_orig:
[The stream is slated to start at noon ET.  Please refresh the page if you do not see a player above.]
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh on Monday highlighted the potential economic benefits of artificial intelligence while warning that the emerging technology also could lead to widespread job losses or fail to deliver on its lofty expectations.
Speaking in San Francisco before a blue-ribbon task force he assembled to examine productivity and employment, the central bank leader stressed that AI "will have significant impact on the economy, with important implications for monetary policy down the road."
"I stress that while I'm not here to offer predictions, I'm not exactly impartial about American leadership in a time so filled with both challenge and possibility," he said in prepared remarks before his productivity and jobs task force.
In his remarks, Warsh used the term "super intelligence" instead of artificial intelligence and described it as "an entirely new force in economic life and society" that has already begun to transform economic activity. President Donald Trump recently ordered that the U.S. government now use the term "super intelligence" almost exclusively instead of AI.
Since taking the Fed chair position, Warsh has emphasized the importance of AI and its potential to improve productivity and ultimately to be a disinflationary force on the economy.
In his remarks Monday,  he noted that AI could lead to productivity gains that could accelerate real economic growth beyond its current range while keeping employment near full capacity. On the downside, he said "less positive" outcomes include job displacement through automation that could raise unemployment.
At the same time, he outlined a third scenario where AI could simply "disappoint."
"After significant capital investment and stock market gains, expected returns could turn down and equity valuations could fall, leading to an economic slowdown and a more notable rise in unemployment," he said. "In time, the economy would recover, but without the productivity gains."
The potential for AI advancement has driven stock market valuations higher and led to companies raising capital to continue competing.
Monday's conference features discussion panels with business leaders, economists and academics. The final session will be a fireside chat that will include Warsh and task force leader and AI advocate Marc Andreessen, co-founder of Andreessen Horowitz.
Warsh created four other task forces addressing topics such as Fed communication, data reliance, balance sheet policy and inflation frameworks.
The chairman noted that this was the first visit he has made to a regional bank.

articles.title_orig: Grand Theft Auto VI launches to rave reviews after 13-year wait
articles.title_zh: Grand Theft Auto VI launches to rave reviews after 13-year wait
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto VI has launched to rave reviews, in one of the most hotly anticipated releases in gaming history.
Gamers got their hands on the latest instalment of the GTA franchise on Thursday, as critics hailed the open-world game as a “masterpiece”, “spectacular”, and an “astonishing American epic”.
The immersive game had an aggregate score of 99 out of 100 on Metacritic, based on more than 150 reviews, as it began dropping on game consoles worldwide from midnight.
“Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played,” critic Luke Reilly wrote in a gushing review for gaming website IGN.
“Accepting that GTA 6 is very much not real also makes it all the more astonishing how much the game is very real,” reviewer Jordan Minor wrote in PCMag.
Grand Theft Auto VI follows the exploits of Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a Bonnie and Clyde-like duo who become entangled in a criminal conspiracy after a seemingly easy score goes awry.
Players have free rein to explore the hyper-realistic fictional state of Leonida and its coastal metropolis of Vice City, stand-ins for Florida and Miami.
Like previous entries in the series, Grand Theft Auto VI features graphic depictions of crime and violence, with players able to mow down pedestrians in stolen vehicles and engage in shootouts with police.
The game, developed by New York-based Rockstar Games at an estimated cost of more than $1bn, is the first instalment in the series since the release of Grand Theft Auto V in 2013.
Originally set to go on sale in 2025, the release was delayed twice to allow developers to polish up gameplay.
Grand Theft Auto VI, which is available on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series, is likely to be the most lucrative release in the history of the gaming industry, which is estimated to be worth some $350bn annually.
Pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto VI exceeded the estimated 15.8 million units as of November 17, generating $1.54bn in revenue, according to market intelligence platform Sensor Tower.
The GTA series began in 1997 with the launch of Grand Theft Auto, a 2D top-down open-world game available on the personal computer, PlayStation and Game Boy Color.

articles.title_orig: A Hunt for Test Cheats With Phone Alerts and Eyeglasses Checks
articles.title_zh: A Hunt for Test Cheats With Phone Alerts and Eyeglasses Checks
articles.content_orig:
South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance exams
The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.
On Thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country. The exam runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects.
The country goes to great lengths to ensure the smooth running of the suneung. Aircraft take-offs and landings are rescheduled during the 25-minute English listening paper to minimise noise, while artillery fire and tank movements are suspended.
The stock market opens an hour late and cars are stopped 200 metres from every centre. Extra trains run from 6am, police drive latecomers to their exam halls, and tourist attractions open late to ease traffic. Offices are asked to open at 10am.
But in recent days, exam organisers have faced a renewed threat to the validity of the entire exercise, after the top scorer in this year’s tax accountancy exam- who got just one question wrong out of 160– admitted on Sunday he had cheated by using AI.
Prime minister Han Seong-sook told a cabinet meeting in Seoul on Tuesday that AI-assisted cheating was a “social evil” that the government would “root out”.
“We will block outright the carrying of smart devices during the exam,” she said. The education ministry and other agencies should approach it “as if staking their jobs on it”, she added.
Han said smart devices must be turned off and handed in, while bags left in corridors would be checked for any devices that were still on. Exam officials would also inspect all candidates’ glasses and watches, as well as their collars, sleeves and buttons for concealed cameras.
The government will also send emergency alerts to every phone in the country, which sound at full volume and cannot be silenced, in the hope of catching out anyone who has not handed in their device.
More invigilators will be deployed, and the government said it was preparing to switch off school wifi inside exam centres and public wifi nearby, and that personal hotspots, which cannot be blocked, would be traced through connection records.
The weekend’s cheating revelation captured national headlines in South Korea , stoking concern about the security of the suneung.
In a video posted to his lawyer’s YouTube channel, the exam cheat said he had photographed the questions with a concealed microcamera, sent them to an AI system and read the answers from a smartphone. “I cheated in the tax accountant exam,” he said. “My top placing is not the result of legitimate effort.”
His lawyer handed police a camera, a laptop and a phone. No charges have been brought, and the prime minister has ordered procedures to begin that would void his result and bar him for five years.
The education minister, Choi Kyo-jin, told parliament on Monday that while authorities could screen out the smart glasses already on sale at Thursday’s exam, newer variants could not be dealt with perfectly.
Choi has ruled out postponing the exam , which has been delayed several times before, including in 2017 , after an earthquake struck the south-eastern city of Pohang, and in 2020 due to the Covid pandemic.
Smart glasses have been banned in exams since the end of June. In October, several candidates were caught with them while sitting university-run admissions exams. At the suneung, wearing a pair counts as using one even when switched off.
The education ministry looked at using radio-frequency equipment to detect the glasses in exam halls, but concluded conditions varied too much between venues for deployment this year. Checks will instead rely on visual inspection, with at least one dedicated official placed in each exam centre.
Teachers’ unions have criticised the government response as belated. A survey last month of 2,716 secondary school teachers by the Korean Teachers and Education Workers Union showed that 82.3% said they could not tell whether a candidate was wearing smart glasses under the current procedure, with only 3.5% saying they could.
To avoid facing scrutiny on exam day, some candidates are reportedly switching to contact lenses. An optician in Suwon, south of Seoul, said students who had never worn contacts were coming in to ask how to put them in.
Han said on X on Monday that the checks would be handled carefully “so that candidates acting in good faith do not suffer unnecessary anxiety or inconvenience”.
In his video confession, the accountancy test cheat addressed suneung candidates directly. “The suneung is coming up soon,” he said.
“To anyone thinking of cheating as I did: I am going to tell the investigators everything, so please don’t think, ‘I won’t get caught.’”

articles.title_orig: Walmart is set to report earnings before the bell. Here's what to expect
articles.title_zh: Walmart is set to report earnings before the bell. Here's what to expect
articles.content_orig:
Walmart is scheduled to report its third fiscal quarter earnings Thursday as the retailer prepares for the holiday season with an increased emphasis on value amid lower consumer sentiment.
The big-box retailer has posted solid growth over the past few quarters as it sees customers gravitate to reduced prices, improvements in delivery and gains in its advertising business. It's also leaned into attracting higher-income consumers with its Walmart+ membership.
Here's what the company is expected to report for its fiscal third quarter, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
Walmart previously said it expects third-quarter net sales to climb 3% to 3.75%. CFO John David Rainey told CNBC last quarter that Walmart's "business is strong" and that he's encouraged by its progress.
The company is typically well insulated from macroeconomic pressures because of its value reputation. Last quarter, the company said it was lowering prices of products across multiple categories, including beef. It also saw a significant boost from tariff refunds, which Rainey said Walmart would use to cut prices.
In October, Walmart announced it was launching a joint membership option with its club subsidiary, Sam's Club, as it leans further into convenience. Both stores will still offer standalone memberships.
The retailer is also rolling out technology in its stores to improve the customer experience, including light-up digital shelf labels that are connected to its app. Those shelf labels and Walmart's AI push have also sparked concerns that the retailer could try to change prices based on demand and shoppers' personal data, which Walmart has denied.
Analysts from UBS wrote in a note last week that they believe the retailer's fiscal third-quarter results will show healthy market share gains.
"E-commerce continues to scale, the company's higher-margin alternative revenue streams continue to grow and Walmart is increasingly able to fund investments in price and convenience while still producing attractive operating income growth," the analysts wrote.
They added that they expect Walmart's fourth-quarter outlook to include "robust operating income growth."
Shares of Walmart have fluctuated this year but are up roughly 13% year-to-date.

articles.title_orig: China's Xi Jinping has orchestrated a remarkable diplomatic moment - but it comes with pitfalls
articles.title_zh: China's Xi Jinping has orchestrated a remarkable diplomatic moment - but it comes with pitfalls
articles.content_orig:
Xi Jinping will believe he has achieved something no other world leader could in securing a historic summit with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen.
For decades, Washington and its western allies shaped the world order.
Yet it is China that has orchestrated the remarkable diplomatic spectacle of three of the world's most powerful protagonists sitting around the table.
And surrounding it all is the futuristic display that is Shenzhen, with driverless cars cruising past as drones fly overhead and robots - literally - dance in the streets.
Ostensibly, this is an economic summit for Asia Pacific leaders. But for Xi, it is also a demonstration of China's grip on the global economy and world politics.
His country is no longer just reacting to decisions made in Washington, London or Brussels - instead Beijing is at the heart of conversations which are reshaping the international order.
But this meeting is not without its pitfalls for Xi as there are many things he does not appear keen to discuss with Putin and Trump.
First, China is not keen for the war in Ukraine, now well into its fifth year, to be on the agenda.
This is a delicate balancing act for Xi who is aware his relationship with Putin may damage China's connections in Europe. The EU is a key market, especially now when the Chinese economy is heavily relying on exports.
However Xi also doesn't want the war to end in a way that will destabilise Russia, a key ally and neighbour.
Beijing is still trying to maintain that it is neutral in this war and has repeatedly called for negotiations and a political settlement while avoiding condemnation of Russia's full-scale invasion.
The US, especially under the previous Biden administration, and Europe have accused China of sending Russia components that it could use in its war in Ukraine, while also propping up the country's economy by buying oil and gas.
Xi wants to keep Putin close, but not too close because he also doesn't want Russia's problems to become China's problems.
Donald Trump has already made it clear he wants the three leaders to discuss limiting the world's supply of nuclear weapons.
The US and Russia possess the world's largest stockpile of nuclear warheads. But China is rapidly expanding its own arsenal, which is raising alarm bells in Washington.
The last major US-Russian arms control treaty, known as New START, expired in February this year, triggering fears of an arms race.  The agreement had set a cap to control the number of nuclear weapons in US and Russia's arsenal.
Trump would like China to be included in any new agreement, but Beijing has pushed back.
Xi's argument will be that his arsenal is considerably smaller than what Washington and Moscow own, and, therefore, it would be unfair for Beijing to be bound by their limits. China also believes it should have the freedom to develop its own nuclear capabilities.
This subject could complicate Xi's bid for China to be recognised as a leader on the world stage - because the US could argue that the status includes being a responsible nuclear power.
Xi will want to control the optics of this meeting, from start to finish.
Chinese officials like to nail down agendas with talking points and produce carefully choreographed speeches.
But in this unprecedented summit, Xi will have to live with two very unpredictable leaders.
Both Trump and Putin have their own agendas and the US President has already threatened to go off script.
There is a risk that they both dominate the meeting and Xi ends up looking like a host, rather than the architect of a major diplomatic moment.
Of course, Xi may be ready for this. It may even play into his hands.
The Chinese leader has been trying to portray himself as a stable global leader - at this summit he will be flanked by two men embroiled in wars they cannot seem to end.
So any unscripted moment could serve to highlight his preferred role as senior statesman.
For all the attention, this meeting of three men with vastly different agendas is unlikely to yield any significant outcomes.
But the power it projects is important for Xi as he heads towards next year's Communist Party Congress, where he is expected to secure a historic fourth term as leader of the party and country.
He may hope to use this as propaganda at home, given the country is grappling with huge domestic challenges.
A country-wide property crisis has dented consumer confidence. Local governments are heavily in debt. Manufacturing has slowed and more of China's workforce has become dependent on flexible jobs with no pension or social security. One in five young people are thought to be struggling to find work. Frustration and anxiety about the future bubble up routinely.
Xi does not have to deal with elections, and the country has not seen major protests in decades. But he will be concerned about his popularity within the party elite as these problems - and the palpable frustrations they produce - grow.
At a time like this, a photo-op with Putin and Trump may offer him proof that his country's "century of humiliation" is over. China is no longer a rising power, he can argue - rather, it is increasingly shaping the rules of a new era.

articles.title_zh: Trump tells Americans concerned over tech outages to ‘relax’ ahead of high-stakes talks in China
articles.content_orig:
The president spoke ahead of meetings with Russia’s Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
• Trump talks tech: President Donald Trump offered a cautiously positive outlook on AI in a speech to Asian leaders in China, saying the new tech required care. In an earlier interview with Fox News, Trump urged Americans concerned about a recent spate of tech outages back home to “relax,” saying the incidents were “individual events.”
• Series of leaders’ talks: Trump will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping separately before their three-way talks later today. A trilateral meeting between the leaders of the US, Russia and China has never happened before.
• Unlikely appearance: Trump hinted that he may meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Shenzhen. But Kim was spotted in his country Wednesday, dampening any prospects of travel to China. Here’s why.
Despite the often fractious relationship between the US and China, President Donald Trump has long lavished his Chinese counterpart with effusive praise – which he continued Thursday at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
“I want to thank President Xi (Jinping) and Madam Peng (Liyuan) for the incredible display that they put forth, last night was unbelievable,” Trump said in opening remarks before the plenary meeting, referring to a welcome banquet held Wednesday night for the attending world leaders.
It’s not the first time he’s flattered Xi, or other authoritarian leaders such as Russian President Vladimir Putin – both of whom the US views, at least on paper, as rivals and possible threats.
As early as his first term, Trump described Xi as “a friend of mine,” a “very special person” and a “very talented man.” And when Xi visited Washington, DC in September, Trump greeted him personally at the airport tarmac, writing afterward that Xi “looks strong, vibrant, and fit - Better than ever.”
On Wednesday, Xi returned the gesture by greeting Trump on the Shenzhen tarmac – a rare break from protocol.
Russia is an “integral” part of the Asia-Pacific region, President Vladimir Putin told APEC leaders in Shenzhen, China Thursday.
In his remarks, the Russian leader urged all regional partners to use Russia’s logistics infrastructure, Reuters reported.
Putin said Russia supports the region’s “energy and food security,” and trade partners can count on Moscow for high-quality and reliable supplies, according to Reuters.
APEC must “unite and build a constructive agenda for cooperation,” Putin added.
As the US increases restrictions on semiconductor exports to curb China’s access to chips, China may also turn to export controls to exercise its own economic leverage.
China holds a near monopoly on the global supply of r are earth metals and minerals , which have become a critical commodity in high-tech supply chains.
The US has already expressed concerns, as recently as this month , that China is not following through on previous trade agreements to grant access to rare earth metals to American companies.
Despite a trade truce reached October 2025 that included China easing export restrictions on rare earths, Chinese exports to the US remained 75% below pre-restriction levels, according to an analysis from the Center for Strategic and International Studies this week.
If the relationship between the two countries deteriorates further, China could use that supply bottleneck to its advantage, some analysts have suggested.
On Monday, the US announced new rules on semiconductor exports to overseas data centers that serve Chinese clients. The change in regulation follows an investigation into one of Nvidia’s biggest customers in Southeast Asia on suspicion that it circumvented export controls and provided advanced US chips to China.
China has warned the US against using the Nvidia controversy, including allegations that the company CEO had an affair with a Chinese intelligence asset, as an excuse to try and hinder China’s technological development.
On Tuesday, China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the latest US restrictions on tech exports “a typical case of economic coercion,” and said it will take necessary measures to safeguard the nation’s interests.
President Donald Trump has floated the idea of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his trip to China.
But North Korea is not a member of the APEC group that is meeting and Kim has not announced any formal plans to attend the summit. And Kim was spotted on his country’s east coast Wednesday , dampening any prospects of that meeting.
Plus, Kim’s peculiar travel habits could make setting up an impromptu meeting between the two leaders difficult — at least in Shenzhen.
The city, located just north of Hong Kong, is more than 1,000 miles from the North Korean border, and Kim rarely flies. Instead, he prefers to travel on his signature armored green train, which moves at the glacial speed of about 37 miles per hour.
The old-fashioned green train has become a symbol of Kim’s dynasty and his secluded nation. It has also long been the subject of intrigue, carrying generations of the Kim family across the country and on rare international trips. Both Kim’s father and grandfather reportedly hosted lavish dinners onboard, featuring live lobster, pork barbecue and wine flown in from France, according to one account.
Kim is no stranger to long international train trips, once taking a 2.5 day journey across China to meet Trump in Hanoi, Vietnam in 2019 for talks on denuclearization. However, that meeting was announced weeks in advance.
Unlike his father, who was reportedly afraid of flying, Kim has traveled by air on rare occasions.
In May 2018, he flew to the Chinese city of Dalian aboard his aging Soviet-made Ilyushin II-2. It was the first international flight taken by a North Korean leader in more than three decades, according to analysts.
Later that year, Kim flew to Singapore on a borrowed Air China Boeing 747 jet to meet Trump.
All eyes are on Xi Jinping’s APEC summit in Shenzhen, and the Chinese leader is using his high-profile moment to send a clear message to countries in the region: stay open to China.
It’s an urgent message for Xi to sell.
China’s economy is heavily reliant on its massive — and increasingly high-tech — export engine, and it’s wary of countries around the world throwing up barriers to protect domestic industries from those goods. That’s especially as China has diversified its trade partners in the face of recent trade frictions with the US.
It’s also keeping a close eye on the US-led Pax Silica initiative, which aims to get countries to agree to keep China out of sensitive AI and digital supply chains, as well as growing calls in America to place more limits on Chinese access to high-tech.
So as Xi and his officials navigate those frictions, ensuring that other nations in the region keep their doors open to China is crucial.
The historic trilateral meeting between President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping, and Russia’s Vladimir Putin set to take place in Shenzhen in China later is front-page news around the world today.
But it barely got a mention on Chinese state media this Thursday morning.
While photos of a smiling Xi standing between Trump and Putin as they shook hands made front pages all over the world, China’s state news agency Xinhua relegated it to its APEC dinner banquet album.
Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning posted the photo to her X account with brief caption “at the dinner banquet.” X is banned in China and there are very few comments on tightly controlled Chinese social media discussing the trilateral meeting.
The muted coverage likely reflects Beijing’s ambivalence about the trilateral talks.
Trump also earlier said he intends to discuss the Ukraine war, and US officials have previously said the three leaders also planned to discuss Iran. Neither topic is one Beijing is willing to make public commitments on.

articles.title_orig: NY faces statewide electricity shortage and has nation's oldest grid
articles.title_zh: NY faces statewide electricity shortage and has nation's oldest grid
articles.content_orig:
There’s gonna be a power struggle!
New York’s overwhelmed energy grid won’t be able to keep up with demand within five years — sparking a blackout crisis and forcing providers to buy energy from out of state, a new report found.
A shortfall of power grids — brought on by outdated infrastructure and the 2021 closure of the Indian Point nuclear plant — could cause a “statewide resource deficiency” by 2032, a report from the New York Independent System Operator (NYISO) released Wednesday found.
That would mean New York City could be forced to mandate planned blackouts across the New York City region and Hudson Valley during high energy usage hours, like overnight during heat waves.
It’s just the latest woeful news out of New York’s beleaguered power system, which has become the third most expensive in the entire country — trailing Hawaii and California, with New York customers being saddled with 10.4% hikes in electricity rates this year through 2028.
“New York’s reliability needs are no longer a distant concern,” said Zach Smith, senior vice president of the NYISO, a nonprofit corporation that operates the Empire State’s bulk electric grid.
“Electricity demand is growing as the availability of reliable power is increasingly uncertain. New generation and transmission resources take years to plan, permit, and build, so the reliability needs identified in this report must be addressed today,” Smith said.
The statewide deficit will reach 1,850 megawatts by 2036, requiring new generation capacity or the state to import power from other states or Canada, the report found.
That deficit is just shy of the roughly 2,000 megawatts that Indian Point in Westchester County generated before it was shuttered by then Gov. Andrew Cuomo. His successor, fellow Democrat Gov. Kathy Hochul, has opposed reopening the plant — despite being forced to slow down her green energy initiatives over rising costs.
But those green initiatives — including sprawling wind farms and a reduction in fossil fuel power plants — aren’t expected to go anywhere in the long run, adding pressure on the state’s energy pinch.
“The state has been blocking new power plants from opening and that’s left New York relying on older, less reliant, less efficient and dirtier units,” Manhattan Institute fellow Ken Girardin told The Post.
“Too much of New York City’s electricity comes from power plants that were built when Dwight Eisenhower was president,” Girardin said, echoing the grid operator’s concerns about New York City’s transmission constraints in particular.
Hochul has blamed New York’s ability to keep up with energy demand on President Trump, whose administration blocked wind projects off the shore of Long Island.
She’s also launched a highly touted effort to develop 1,000 new megawatts of nuclear power plant electricity generating capacity under a so-called “master plan” released by her administration Wednesday.
Despite including 12 technical studies – over 1,000 pages – the taxpayer-funded wonks at the New York state Energy Research and Development Authority never bothered to mention a timeline for actually bringing a new power plant online in the plan. Hochul’s office wouldn’t provide a date either.
Not to mention that the grid operator specifically notes that the problem facing New York City ahead of 2032 is a throttle in transmission, meaning opening a new power plant anywhere upstate wouldn’t solve the problem on its own.
